definitions.meaning: The smallest unit of life; every living thing is made of one or more cells, each carrying the structures it needs to stay alive.
A tough outer layer found in plant cells only. It gives the cell its shape and strength but is fully permeable.
The thin layer around every cell that controls what enters and leaves. It is selectively permeable.
Letting some substances through while keeping others out - the membrane chooses, like a gatekeeper.
The control centre of the cell, holding the instructions that run everything the cell does.
The plant-only structure that traps light energy to make food by photosynthesis.
A fluid-filled space. In plant cells it is large and permanent; filled with water it pushes the cell firm.
The structure that releases energy from food, in both plant and animal cells.
The jelly-like substance inside the cell where most of its work happens.
A plant cell swollen firm because its full vacuole pushes the membrane against the wall.
A group of similar cells working together at the same job, such as leaf tissue.
A structure made of several tissues working together, such as a leaf or a heart.
A group of organs working together, such as the shoot system or the circulatory system.

mechanismSteps: A plant cell, labelled - wall outside, membrane inside it, then nucleus, chloroplast and the large vacuole: the full plant kit.
An animal cell, labelled - membrane, nucleus and mitochondrion only: no wall, no chloroplast, no large vacuole.
The membrane is the gatekeeper - food crosses in, waste crosses out, and a harmful particle is refused: the membrane chooses.
Two specialists: nucleus and chloroplast - the nucleus controls the cell with its instructions, the chloroplast traps light to make food.
Why plants stand up straight - a full vacuole pushes the membrane against the wall so the cell is turgid; lose water and it goes flaccid.
Cells team up: the organisation ladder - cell to tissue to organ to system, as in leaf cell to leaf tissue to leaf to shoot system.
objectives: Label the main structures of plant and animal cells and state each job
Explain the cell membrane as selectively permeable, not a solid wall
Describe turgor in a plant cell and order the organisation ladder from cell to system
subject: science
title: Cells: structure and organisation

trap.explanation: The slip: A wall feels like protection, so the membrane is read as a barrier that stops everything. The fix: The membrane is selectively permeable: it lets some things through and keeps others out. In class, replay the gatekeeper scene: the food particle crossing in is the proof - if the membrane blocked everything, the cell would take in no food and remove no waste, and it would die.
trap.misconception: The cell membrane is a solid wall that blocks everything from entering or leaving.

workedExample: Read the ladder, then test the gatekeeper. Step 1 (s6): group a leaf cell with its neighbours to make leaf tissue, the tissue builds the leaf organ, and the leaf joins the shoot system. Step 2 (s3): a food particle crosses the membrane while a harmful one is refused, so the cell stays turgid-fed and protected - a wall could do neither job.
